portInfo.description: Puerto Bahías de Huatulco, under ASIPONA Salina Cruz, is described by the authority as a fundamentally tourism-oriented harbour whose operations concentrate on cruise ships and cruise passengers, marinas and local nautical tourism. The Programa Maestro de Desarrollo Portuario (PMDP) 2022–2027 details specialised cruise infrastructure: a finger pier with two berths totalling 450 m of berthing length (180 m concrete-pile platform plus two 153.10 m breasting dolphins), a passenger-and-authorities terminal building, and 9.0 m official draft on the cruise approach and basins. Cruise is named the port’s principal business line; the PMDP notes pandemic-era collapse and a 2021 movement of 18.3 thousand passengers during early recovery — treat that figure as year-specific, not a current forecast.

thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: If your ship’s LOA/draft or schedule forces tendering, rebuild the day around tender queues — the PMDP explicitly contemplates ship’s-boat transfers when the pier cannot take the vessel.
